video_title: Robinhood Chain's Memecoin Boom + Tokenized Stocks - The Chopping Block
gist: Robinhood Chain saw a second, much larger activity surge (125k+ active wallets, $1.2B DEX volume, 5.7M daily txns) driven by OHM-fork memecoins bonded to tokenized stocks (e.g. Boner/HIMS, Cinema/AMC) that inadvertently boosted RWA issuance from near-zero to ~$70-80M, while structurally transferring money from weekend retail buyers to arbitrageurs; the panel also debates whether this dethrones Solana, and dissects Hyperliquid's reported onshore JV with Kraken/Bitnomial as a preview of a lasting bifurcation between regulated domestic crypto venues and offshore global liquidity.

insights.claim: In its second rally, Robinhood Chain hit over 125,000 active wallets, 5.7 million transactions per day, $1.2 billion in DEX volume, and $2 million in REV (fee revenue) in a single day, a much larger surge than its initial launch spike.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: A concrete, dated on-chain activity spike investors can use to size how much real economic activity (vs. hype) Robinhood Chain is generating; watch whether these levels are sustained past the weekend meme cycle.
insights.quote: We are now seeing over 125,000 active wallets, 5.7 million transactions per day, $1.2 billion in DEX volume, 2 million in REV in a single day.

insights.claim: Robinhood Chain's TVL is only $730 million (ranking it ~11th among chains), yet it ranks #2 by 24-hour DEX volume behind Solana, meaning a very small pool of assets is turning over extremely fast.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: High volume-to-TVL ratio signals speculative/degenerate trading velocity rather than deep, sticky liquidity — a red flag for durability of the activity once the meme cycle cools.

insights.claim: On a 30-day basis Solana still leads all chains in DEX volume at roughly $62 billion vs. Robinhood Chain's ~$17 billion and Ethereum's ~$33 billion, but on the most recent day Robinhood Chain ($1.5B) had overtaken Ethereum ($1.3B) and was closing in on Solana ($2.5B) in daily volume.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: Shows Robinhood Chain's momentum is very recent and concentrated — useful for timing whether this is a sustained share shift or a short-lived spike.

insights.claim: Roughly 90,000 of the 125,000 active Robinhood Chain wallets reportedly originated from the FOMO trading app, while by trading volume the activity splits roughly 50/50 between FOMO and GMGN, implying GMGN users are far fewer but trade in much larger size (more professional/bot-like) than the mostly retail FOMO user base.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Distinguishes retail-driven wallet growth from professional/bot-driven volume — investors should discount headline wallet counts as a pure retail-adoption signal since much of the dollar volume is being captured by sophisticated 'sharks,' not new normie users.
insights.quote: It was like 90,000 of 125,000 addresses were from originated from FOMO.

insights.claim: Almost none of Robinhood Chain's user growth is coming through Robinhood's own native app — it is being driven almost entirely by third-party front-ends (FOMO, GMGN), meaning the aggregator/wallet layer, not the chain or the brokerage itself, may be capturing the real long-term distribution value.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (Unchained host, guest)
insights.so_what: If distribution value accrues to wallet/aggregator apps rather than to the underlying chain, that changes who the investable winner is in this ecosystem — watch FOMO/GMGN-style front ends as potential value capture points independent of which chain they route to.

insights.claim: Memecoin traders are no longer loyal to any single blockchain — wallet-abstraction apps like FOMO route users across chains transparently, so users increasingly don't know or care which chain they're trading on.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Erodes the chain-loyalty moat that Solana previously enjoyed with memecoin traders; implies future speculative flow will chase whichever chain has the best current mechanism/incentive, not brand loyalty — a bearish structural signal for chain-specific network effects.
insights.quote: Memecoin traders are not loyal to a chain anymore. That was the first lesson I got from this.

themes.theme: Value capture: L2s win, L1s barely capture fees

insights.claim: Robinhood Chain is built on the Arbitrum stack and kicks back fees to Robinhood, which drove a rally in Arbitrum, while Ethereum L1 only earns small data-availability fees for publishing data rather than capturing any of the actual transaction/trading fee value.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: Concrete real-world evidence for the 'L2s extract value, L1s don't capture it' bear case on Ethereum's fee-capture thesis — worth weighing against ETH's other value accrual narratives (security, DA demand growth).

insights.claim: Robinhood reportedly came very close to launching its chain on Solana around late 2024 and only switched to Arbitrum at the last minute; the deciding factor was believed to be that running your own L2 lets you keep transaction fee revenue instead of paying another chain for it.
insights.speaker: Tom (Chopping Block co-host)
insights.so_what: A near-miss counterfactual: had Robinhood built on Solana, the recent activity/liquidity surge would likely have accrued to Solana instead — illustrates how fee-capture economics, not just technical merit, now drive large issuers' L1/L2 chain choice.

insights.claim: A wave of OHM-fork protocols (with modified contracts) turned memecoins into a bonding/liquidity incentive for minting tokenized stocks: to mint a memecoin you must bond an underlying tokenized stock (e.g., put in $100 of stock, get $10 of memecoin locked as LP liquidity and $90 back), effectively making the memecoin a token incentive for growing RWA (real-world asset) issuance and liquidity.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A genuinely novel mechanism worth tracking: using degenerate memecoin speculation as bootstrap liquidity/demand for tokenized real-world assets, something years of dedicated RWA projects failed to achieve organically.
insights.quote: The stock pairing basically makes a memecoin almost like a token incentive for an individual stock.

insights.claim: The memecoin 'Boner' was paired with HIMS (Hims & Hers) tokenized stock on Robinhood Chain, and the memecoin 'Cinema' was paired with AMC's tokenized stock; both tokenized stocks deviated (depegged) sharply from the real underlying stock price over the weekend when equity markets were closed.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Concrete named examples of the mechanism in action and evidence that tokenized-stock pegs break down materially during periods when the reference market (Wall Street) is closed but the on-chain venue keeps trading.
insights.quote: Cinema... Monday morning market opened and it dep so badly and like the tokenized stock was just trading way below the real one for a long time.

insights.claim: The mechanism systematically transfers wealth from weekend retail buyers to arbitrageurs and hedge funds: retail FOMO-buys the memecoin as its paired tokenized stock runs up over the weekend disconnected from the real stock, and when normal trading (and minting/arbitrage) resumes Monday, those who can run the arbitrage between the tokenized price and real stock price profit at retail's expense.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (Unchained host, guest)
insights.so_what: This is a structural, near-guaranteed-loss mechanism for retail participants (not just high-variance gambling) — an important distinction for anyone evaluating whether to treat these RWA-memecoin pairs as speculative bets versus mechanically rigged trades favoring sophisticated arbitrageurs.
insights.quote: You are handing all this money in this big massive depeg to like hedge funds and that's the thing that everyone's getting so excited about.

insights.claim: Total RWA (tokenized equity) issuance/minting on Robinhood Chain went from near-zero (sub a few million dollars) to roughly $70-80 million, up about 50% week-over-week, driven almost entirely by small retail-sized ($5-$10) memecoin-driven minting rather than the whale-dominated issuance typical of most RWA platforms.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A memecoin gambling mechanism accomplished in one weekend what dedicated RWA distribution efforts had failed to do for years (retail-scale organic RWA minting) — worth monitoring whether this issuance sticks or evaporates once the meme fades.
insights.quote: Before they had like basically no minting there was like sub a few million total... over the weekend on Robin[hood]... look, they came for the boners, they leave for the hymns.

insights.claim: The broader tokenized public-equity market (Ondo, B-stocks, xStocks combined) is roughly $3-4 billion in size, meaning Robinhood Chain's ~$70-80 million in new RWA issuance, while a large relative jump for the chain, is still a small fraction of total tokenized-equity market cap.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Right-sizes the RWA-memecoin story: it's a meaningful bootstrap for Robinhood Chain specifically, not yet a market-moving event for the tokenized-equities sector overall.

insights.claim: This memecoin mania generated more Uniswap v4 hook usage than Uniswap v4 had seen in its entire prior existence, despite no new smart contract code being written — it was a remix/mashup of existing DeFi primitives (OHM forks, Uniswap v4 hooks) rather than genuine innovation.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Demonstrates that speculative/meme-driven demand, not developer-led innovation, is currently the strongest driver of adoption for existing DeFi infrastructure — a signal for where usage (and possibly fee revenue) is concentrating in the current cycle.
insights.quote: This meme mania got much more Uniswap v4 hook usage than Uniswap got in its entire time.

insights.claim: The specific stock-memecoin bonding mechanism is expected to have a short half-life (a couple of weekends) once participants realize the structural losing dynamic, but the broader 'meta' of pairing memecoins with RWAs as an incentive/distribution mechanism is expected to continue and be copied by new projects.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: Actionable framing for tracking the trend: don't expect any single RWA-meme pair to last, but expect a steady stream of new ones as the 'memecoin-grifter supply chain' redeploys the mechanic onto new tokenized assets — watch for copycat launches as an ongoing (if declining-quality) flow driver.
insights.quote: You only need a couple weekends before people realize, oh, don't do this one... but the meta of, oh, find a memecoin and attach it to some RWA, that's definitely going to continue.

themes.theme: Memecoins as entertainment vs. deceptive gambling — the ethics debate

insights.claim: A legitimate casino is honest that players are gambling and will likely lose, whereas memecoin platforms and influencers let buyers believe they are 'making money' through legitimate investing rather than gambling — this deception, not the losses themselves, is the core harm.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: A reusable ethical/regulatory framework for evaluating any speculative crypto product: the presence of honest disclosure (casino-style) vs. implied investment-return framing (memecoin-influencer style) is the key distinction regulators and allocators should focus on, not simply whether people can lose money.
insights.quote: The problem is not that people are losing money. It's that they think they're making money. That's the problem.

insights.claim: Pump.fun buyer data from 2025 showed roughly 95% of buyers lost money, evidence used to argue that memecoin trading is a near-guaranteed-loss activity for the vast majority of retail participants, not a fair-odds speculative bet.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: Hard base-rate data point for sizing retail memecoin losses across the 2025 cycle — useful reference stat when assessing consumer-protection or platform-liability risk in memecoin-adjacent products.
insights.quote: We saw what happened over... pump[.fun] buyers over the course of 2025. It's like 95% of people lost money.

insights.claim: The current RWA-memecoin mania is best understood as a generational/cultural phenomenon — a mashup of DeFi Summer creativity, GameStop-style retail mania, and 'financial jackass'-style entertainment-through-losing-money — rather than as a rational financial strategy, and this pattern (new primitive, new speculative game, same underlying irrationality) recurs every crypto cycle.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (Unchained host, guest)
insights.so_what: Useful lens for anticipating future cycles: expect each new crypto primitive (this cycle: RWAs) to be quickly repurposed into a new speculative 'game' regardless of whether the underlying primitive has real utility — position for the pattern, not just the current mechanism.
insights.quote: Crypto has this way... anytime there's a new primitive, crypto finds a way to remix it and create a new game.

insights.claim: Unlike prior bear-market memecoin waves where crypto sentiment collapsed alongside retail memecoin losses regardless of positive fundamentals (stablecoin adoption, the GENIUS Act, spot ETFs), traders in the trenches losing money don't care about macro/fundamental improvements — sentiment tracks personal trading P&L, not industry-level facts.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (Unchained host, guest)
insights.so_what: Explains the disconnect between strong on-chain/regulatory fundamentals and weak retail crypto sentiment — sentiment indicators tied to retail speculative P&L may be more predictive of near-term market mood than fundamental/regulatory news flow.
insights.quote: It doesn't matter what the facts are. It's like if you were in the trenches and you were losing money constantly, you were going to feel down bad... The fact that crypto is in a better position than ever just doesn't matter.

themes.theme: Solana vs. Robinhood Chain: is this a changing of the guard?

insights.claim: A commentator (Flood) argued Solana is 'in the most perilous place it's ever been since its inception,' citing that Robinhood Chain is now capturing the RWA/memecoin mania that historically went to Solana, Solana has almost no purpose-built exchange with meaningful market share, almost no RWA market share, and many of its trading pairs are shifting from SOL to stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: A bear thesis on Solana's ecosystem moat worth stress-testing against the volume data (Solana still leads 30-day DEX volume) — the panel is split on whether this is a real structural shift or a temporary spike.
insights.quote: Salana is in the most perilous place it's ever been since its inception.

insights.claim: Solana arguably fumbled its RWA/tokenized-stock first-mover advantage: it heavily subsidized xStocks liquidity and activity on Solana, but then let the xStocks relationship get acquired by Kraken, losing the alignment/loyalty it had paid to build.
insights.speaker: Tom (Chopping Block co-host)
insights.so_what: A cautionary case study on ecosystem incentive design: subsidizing a third-party product without securing long-term alignment/ownership can let a competitor (or acquirer) capture the value the subsidy created — relevant when evaluating any chain's ecosystem-grant strategy.
insights.quote: I actually think um... the biggest bungling I think was negotiating the XStocks relationship with Salana... and then they let it get purchased by Kraken.

insights.claim: Despite the Robinhood Chain surge, Solana remains the largest chain by both TVL ($5.7B, more than 7x Robinhood Chain's $730M) and 30-day DEX volume (~$62B), suggesting the panel should be cautious about declaring a changing of the guard based on one or two days of data.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: A grounding counterpoint to the 'Solana is dying' narrative — useful for investors to avoid overreacting to short-term daily volume flips when underlying liquidity depth still favors Solana by a wide margin.
insights.quote: It's important not to grave dance too early because Salana still... is still the number one chain by DEX volume by a pretty wide margin.

insights.claim: Because wallet-abstraction apps like FOMO make traders indifferent to which chain they're using, chain-level competitive outcomes may increasingly be decided by which application/wallet layer wins distribution, not by which base-layer chain has technical superiority or first-mover status.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (Unchained host, guest)
insights.so_what: Reframes the investable unit of competitive advantage from 'chain' to 'front-end/aggregator app' — worth tracking which wallet/app layers are consolidating user distribution across chains rather than betting purely on chain-level moats.

insights.claim: Founders/ecosystems that were early to a category but lost execution or negotiating leverage tend to become the most bitter about later entrants capturing the win — drawn as a recurring crypto pattern (the biggest DEX and biggest prediction market were not the first movers in their categories either).
insights.speaker: Tom (Chopping Block co-host)
insights.so_what: A pattern-recognition heuristic for investors: being first in a crypto category is a weak predictor of who ultimately captures the market — weight execution and distribution partnerships over chronological priority when evaluating competing ecosystems/products.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid's reported onshore push via Kraken/Bitnomial

insights.claim: Bloomberg reported Hyperliquid Labs is in advanced talks with Kraken's parent company, Payward, for a potential joint venture that would let Hyperliquid use Bitnomial's regulated license and clearing house to bring a KYC'd, onshore US product to market, with some kind of liquidity bridging from Hyperliquid's main order book; neither party confirmed the report.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: Concrete near-term regulatory/market-structure event to track — an onshore, CFTC-compliant Hyperliquid product would be a significant milestone for bringing perp DEX-style trading into the regulated US market.

insights.claim: On the news of the reported Hyperliquid-Kraken/Payword talks, CME's stock price fell while Hyperliquid's token price rose, indicating the market is pricing a credible competitive threat to CME's derivatives franchise from a regulated onshore Hyperliquid product.
insights.speaker: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly, host)
insights.so_what: A direct market read-through: traditional derivatives exchanges (CME) are already being priced as at-risk incumbents versus onshore-regulated crypto perp venues — worth monitoring CME/Hyperliquid as a pair trade on regulatory developments.

insights.claim: An onshore, KYC'd Hyperliquid product (potentially still branded as a HIP-3 market) would necessarily differ structurally from the offshore DeFi product because US regulation requires centralized clearing, different collateral/margin rules, and different liquidation mechanisms (no automatic ADL as done in DeFi) plus prime-broker and market-surveillance infrastructure — meaning it will feel like a fundamentally different product to institutional/advanced traders even if retail barely notices the difference.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations for any 'onshore DeFi' launch: don't expect true feature/liquidity parity with the offshore version — the regulated version is a structurally distinct product, which matters for institutional users evaluating counterparty and collateral risk differently than retail.
insights.quote: It's going to end up... having a totally different feel to advanced trader... for institutional traders it's going to be quite a different experience.

insights.claim: Track records of prior offshore-to-US-branded exchange launches (FTX US, OKX's US entity, Huobi's US attempt, Binance US) have largely been disappointing — none achieved dominant US market share, suggesting brand transfer alone doesn't guarantee onshore success and Hyperliquid's onshore venture faces the same execution risk.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A base-rate caution for evaluating Hyperliquid's onshore prospects: prior 'bring the offshore brand onshore' plays have mostly failed to gain real US share, so investors should not assume Hyperliquid's brand alone secures a strong onshore outcome.
insights.quote: All these international foreign exchanges trying to land in the US, it's just a graveyard.

insights.claim: Polymarket's dual-product approach (global Polymarket vs. regulated Polymarket US) is offered as the working precedent: despite criticism, both versions have grown even though they are very different products/experiences, suggesting Hyperliquid's onshore/offshore split could similarly coexist and both grow rather than one cannibalizing the other.
insights.speaker: Tom (Chopping Block co-host)
insights.so_what: A relevant comparable for modeling how a Hyperliquid onshore/offshore split might play out commercially — Polymarket US growth despite skepticism is a bullish precedent for the viability of parallel regulated/unregulated product lines.

insights.claim: Long-term, crypto markets may bifurcate permanently into per-jurisdiction regulated/onshore venues versus a persistent offshore/global liquidity layer, analogous to China's walled-off internet versus the global internet — full convergence onto one global standard is unlikely because governments have strong incentives (capital-flight control, legal/collateral-rights differences such as being able to sue a centralized clearing agent but not an on-chain protocol) to keep their markets separate.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A macro market-structure thesis with long horizon implications: don't expect a single unified global crypto liquidity venue to emerge — instead expect a persistent parallel structure of regulated domestic venues plus offshore global venues, similar to how equities already diverge by jurisdiction (e.g., different rules across US, LSE, JPX, and how ADRs of the same stock trade differently across markets).
insights.quote: I think it's really hard to imagine those systems coexisting in a like collateral identical way... local governments have a lot of incentive to really disincentivize that because they do want control over a lot of asset capital flight stuff.

insights.claim: Crypto is expected to bring 'informal markets' (technically restricted but practically tolerated activity) to jurisdictions like the US the way they already exist in countries like China, where individuals can access banned platforms via workarounds with little enforcement risk unless they are a large, visible entity — implying retail users will keep accessing offshore venues like Hyperliquid Global even as regulated entities are confined to onshore versions.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Suggests onshore regulation will primarily constrain institutional/regulated players rather than eliminate retail access to offshore venues — regulatory arbitrage by individual users is likely to persist regardless of new onshore product launches.
insights.quote: If you're a regulated entity, you're not going to be trading on Hyperliquid Global... But if you're a retail user, you probably will... And if it's not Hyperliquid, there will be a next thing.

themes.theme: Cultural divergence in speculative trading: US vs. Asia

insights.claim: At an Asia crypto conference, numerous founders pitched localized ('FOMO for Asia') social-trading apps on the premise that American entertainment-oriented apps like FOMO don't resonate in Asia, arguing Asian users want to make money rather than be entertained by watching streams and losing money.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Signals a wave of Asia-localized memecoin/social-trading app launches to watch for — but also a market thesis (entertainment vs. profit framing) that could determine which apps actually gain traction regionally.
insights.quote: We need a FOMO for Asia because... Asian users don't use FOMO... FOMO is too American.

insights.claim: Observed cultural difference in trading psychology: Chinese/Asian crypto traders tend to frame trading as needing to identify who they are 'dumping on' to ensure they profit, while American traders more often frame it as a collective 'we're all going to get rich together' (and beat the hedge funds) mentality.
insights.speaker: Tom (Chopping Block co-host)
insights.so_what: A soft but potentially useful behavioral-finance lens for designing or evaluating region-specific trading products — apps built on 'community upside' narratives may underperform in markets where the dominant mental model is explicitly zero-sum.
insights.quote: I feel like they're like okay tell me who's losing money... Whereas in America it's like well none of us are going to lose money. We're all just going to beat the hedge funds.

insights.claim: GMGN, one of the two dominant front-ends driving Robinhood Chain volume, is believed to be a largely Chinese-built/staffed team, which the panel connects to why it lacks the social/streamer/tipping features found in more entertainment-oriented apps aimed at Western retail users.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Useful color for understanding why GMGN skews toward higher-volume, more professionalized traders rather than entertainment-driven retail flow — relevant when evaluating GMGN vs. FOMO as investment or partnership targets.
